request: hey walk me through readme of this repo

questions.ask: This repo doesn't actually have a README file right now — do you want me to create one, or would you rather I just explain the repo to you here in the chat?
questions.why: determines whether this becomes a code change (writing a new file) or just a conversational answer with no file added

questions.ask: If we create a README, should it just be a quick 'how to run it' guide, or also cover things like what the app does, its API, and how tests work?
questions.why: determines how long/detailed the README content and sections should be

questions.ask: Who is this README mainly for — other developers setting the project up, or someone non-technical trying to understand what the app does?
questions.why: determines the tone and level of technical detail (setup commands vs. plain-language overview)

findings.note: No README or README.md file exists anywhere in the repo — the user's premise of an existing README to 'walk through' is incorrect
Project is named 'todo-app', v0.1.0, Node >=22, uses Express; scripts: npm run seed (seed db), npm start (run server), npm test (playwright tests)
Simple Express + SQLite backend for a todo list: GET/POST /api/tasks, PATCH /api/tasks/:id to toggle done, serves static files from public/, health check at /health
Defines how this harness sets up/starts/checks the app (./scripts/setup-app, start-app, check-app) and records journeys; readiness check hits http://127.0.0.1:3000/health
Other top-level dirs: db/ (sqlite db + seed), public/ (static frontend), tests/, journeys/, scripts/ — consistent with a small full-stack todo app
